stem: Why is a clean-to-dirty work sequence useful in cultivation biosecurity?
choices: It reduces the chance of carrying pests or pathogens from higher-risk areas into cleaner areas
It makes plants grow faster because workers move in one direction
It eliminates the need for tool sanitation
It is required only during harvest
rationale: Working from cleaner or lower-risk material toward dirtier or known-problem areas helps reduce movement of biological hazards into cleaner crop zones.
